title: Voice input in noisy and shared environments
bottleneck: Voice is natural but fails in noise, wind, and crowds, and speaking commands aloud is socially awkward and privacy-leaking in public. Recognition accuracy collapses with accents, overlapping speech, and domain jargon. Silent-speech alternatives (EMG, ultrasound) are immature.
why_it_blocks: AR glasses need discreet input for public use; if voice only works alone in quiet rooms, it's not a mobile interface. The social and acoustic realities of the world defeat voice.
current_state: On-device speech recognition is fast and private in good conditions; beamforming mics help in moderate noise. Robust, discreet voice in real-world chaos is still unreliable. Speaking commands aloud broadcasts potentially sensitive queries to everyone nearby, a privacy cost most users will not pay. On-device recognition helps privacy but cannot fix the fundamental social awkwardness of talking to glasses.
